articles.title: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
articles.summaryTr: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
articles.articleText: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own - Published Pope Leo XIV has celebrated Mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago. Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the Mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C. For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight. "The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth Díaz, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023. Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff, who was elected in May 2025. The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance. The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities. Around Chiclayo, it is hard to meet anyone who doesn't claim to be a friend of the Pope or have a special anecdote about him. Some recall how he would enjoy sampling Peruvian delicacies at El Trébol, a restaurant next to the city's cathedral. Others remember his love of tennis. But for many it's the more serious moments of his time here, such as helping launch soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic, or wading through deep waters on horseback when floods hit the area. Several of these images are on display in a small museum dedicated to him at the entrance to the bishop's residence. But for the city, and for a country that calls him the "Peruvian Pope", his return home means much more than a collection of photographs and anecdotes. "It is the return of the man who brought Peruvians closer to the Church," said Samuel David Miranda Atoche, a local parish priest from Chiclayo who was ordained by the Pope back when he was still the bishop and known under his birth name of Robert Prevost. And it is not just local people he connected with, according to Díaz, who came to Chiclayo from Venezuela. "It was difficult for him to see so many migrants living on the streets," she added, recalling the time when large numbers of Venezuelans came through Chiclayo escaping the political and economic crisis in their home country. "So, he got in touch with the migration authorities and coordinated with other organisations to speed up the paperwork needed for many of us to obtain legal residency and work permits." - Who is Robert Prevost, the new Pope Leo XIV? - Published9 May 2025 Robert Prevost's time here as bishop also involved difficult decisions, such as having to deal with the controversy and scandal surrounding the dissolution of Sodalitium of Christian Life, a Peruvian Catholic organisation that had faced decades of sexual abuse allegations. Santiago Roncagliolo, a Peruvian writer and journalist who has studied the Pope's life, believes his handling of that crisis earned him the favour of his predecessor, Pope Francis, and helped set him on the path to the papacy. Father Miranda also stressed the role the now-pontiff played in bringing people together. "If there is one thing Bishop Prevost worked for here," he added, referring to the Pope by his previous title, "it was unity". That unity has been on display in the run up to the Mass, with the square in front of Chiclayo Cathedral filled with joyous celebrations for days. Normally, 800,000 people live in the city and its surrounding area, but estimates say the Pope's visit has caused that to double. Local businesses have been capitalising on the Pope's popularity to boost sales and hotels have sharply increased their nightly room rates. But that didn't seem to put off the faithful who gathered for the Mass. Shouts of: "The Pope is from Chiclayo!" echoed across the field during the event. Their affection was clearly reflected by the pontiff. "As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart," he said from the stage, "for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life." articles.summary: Bitcoin sales, valuation losses and rising borrowing costs weighed on the Japanese company’s earnings despite higher revenue and operating profit.

articles.titleTr: Metaplanet swings to $170M loss as Bitcoin sale hits earnings
articles.summaryTr: Bitcoin sales, valuation losses and rising borrowing costs weighed on the Japanese company’s earnings despite higher revenue and operating profit.
articles.articleText: Metaplanet swings to $170M loss as Bitcoin sale hits earnings Bitcoin sales, valuation losses and rising borrowing costs weighed on the Japanese company’s earnings despite higher revenue and operating profit. Metaplanet swung to a $170 million net loss in the first nine months of 2026, hit by a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings and a loss on the sale of 10,000 coins to demonstrate its ability to raise cash. The Japanese company, the world’s second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, posted a net loss of 27.16 billion yen (about $170 million), compared with a profit of 13.53 billion yen ($84.6 million) in the same period last year. A 19.17 billion yen ($119.8 million) loss on the Bitcoin sale and an 8.04 billion yen ($50.3 million) loss from a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings outweighed gains in the operating business. Over the quarter, Metaplanet sold the 10,000 BTC for 124.7 billion yen and temporarily held the proceeds in cash, stablecoins and other liquid assets. It then spent 149.9 billion yen to buy 11,000 BTC, paying 9.3% more per coin on average. The company said the sale was meant to show rating agencies and bond investors that it could turn its Bitcoin into cash to meet financing obligations. At the end of September, holdings rose by a net 1,000 coins to 44,000 BTC. Top 10 largest Bitcoin treasury companies. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.NET Metaplanet borrowed against its Bitcoin holdings during the quarter, increasing the amount it owed under the credit line to $649.5 million at the end of September from $414 million at the end of June. The company said it funded Bitcoin purchases from the second quarter onward with money borrowed under the credit line, proceeds from bond sales and the exercise of stock acquisition rights, and revenue from its Bitcoin options business. Metaplanet’s interest expense rose 56% from the previous quarter to 1.36 billion yen ($8.5 million). Short-term borrowings and bonds payable totaled 110.5 billion yen ($691 million) at the end of September. For the nine months through September, revenue rose 30.5% to 5.9 billion yen ($36.9 million), while operating profit increased 26.5% to 3.48 billion yen ($21.8 million). The company cut its full-year revenue forecast to 6.5 billion yen ($40.6 million) from 16 billion yen ($100 million). Related: Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal Bitcoin treasury companies face pressure from falling prices, index removals Metaplanet’s earnings come as Bitcoin treasury companies face mounting pressure from incoming stock index removals and falling Bitcoin prices. Index provider MSCI confirmed Wednesday that Strategy, Metaplanet and Upexi would be removed from its equity indexes at the Nov. 30 market close, potentially prompting funds that track those benchmarks to sell the shares. JPMorgan previously estimated that Strategy’s removal could result in roughly $2.8 billion in selling pressure from MSCI-linked funds. Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday and was trading around $68,600 as of 4:51 p.m. UTC, down about 9% over the previous week, according to CoinGecko data. articles.title: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9325-26 CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced that it has filed a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state’s attempts to halt event-contract trading and impose up to hundreds of millions of dollars in civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is bringing a civil enforcement against Kalshi in state court, a CFTC-designated contract market. Arkansas’s efforts to obstruct the functions of CFTC-registered exchanges operating lawfully under the Commodity Exchange Act are preempted by federal law. “As prediction markets continue to prove their value in being useful for risk management and providing the public with valuable information about the future, Arkansas seeks to shut down event contracts ranging from sports and politics to other important world events,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act, and the Commission will not let state interference thwart its regulatory efforts and destroy federally regulated markets.” Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued to vindicate federal sovereign interests. The CFTC has also submitted amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
news.summary: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
news.summaryTr: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.
news.articleText: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion? - Published In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass. Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him. More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends. Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with. But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward. "He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma. Jojo was less than a year old – an infant clinging to his mother – when he was captured and sold. Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him. Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction". "He will even go to the trouble of gathering leaves for us to hold, so that we [trade them] for a treat – to interact with us," he says. Jojo also calls out when women he knows well visit his enclosure and then leave, making sounds that silverback males use to summon the females in the wild, explains Éric Willaume, who runs the sanctuary. "He definitely feels lonely," he says. Jojo is one of the more than 6,000 African primates estimated to have been bought or sold in the global trade of apes and other primates between 2000 and 2023. Thousands more are trafficked illegally for use as exotic pets, wild meat, and traditional medicine, the Pan African Sanctuary Alliance says., external Experts believe when baby great apes are taken from their group at a young age like Jojo, they are left traumatised. "If they're old enough to understand what happened to them, to understand their family was killed, they just lose the will to live," explains conservationist Tony King, from UK charity the Aspinall Foundation. "You see it in their eyes – the light goes out. I never knew where that expression came from, but I've seen it in gorillas." King – who specialises in rehabilitating rescued great apes – remembers rescuing two infant sister gorillas who were brought to a sanctuary in the Congo Basin. "They were clinging to each other," he says. "They stayed together in a little tight ball for about three days before they sort of unravelled. I think that's what kept them alive." African charity the Gorilla Rehabilitation and Conservation Education (Grace) Center uses what it calls "gorilla-led" rehabilitation. When the team rescues a young gorilla from the pet trade, they put it with a group as soon as possible so they can socialise and essentially learn to be a gorilla. But Jojo's case is unusual. He is fully mature and showing signs of harmful, chronic stress, according to Forrester. In a game-changing approach to studying anxiety and trauma in apes, she has used a thermal camera to film Jojo's face. This allows her to monitor blood flow, revealing what appears to be a chronically cold nose. It's a sign of a malfunctioning stress response. When any primate – a human, chimp or gorilla - is stressed, blood flow to the eyes and ears increases. It puts them on high alert for danger, but leaves their nose, temporarily, colder. For Jojo, this "nasal dip" as it is known, does not seem to recover. "Being connected to others is incredibly important to our psychology as great apes," Forrester says. "Having another individual to share his life with would be so healing for him. "I would assume other gorillas would help him process this grief and trauma." Dr Katie Fawcett, from the Grace Center, says it's also "essential" for an animal to form social relationships to be considered for release into the wild - which is the ultimate goal for Jojo's keepers. The bonds between gorillas – what we would call friendship - is key to their society, adds Dr Robin Morrison from the University of Zurich, who studies the social lives of mountain gorillas. In one recent study, she discovered that female mountain gorillas would seek out females they knew, even if they hadn't seen them for many years, when joining a group. And she says a big part of a gorilla's normal social life is "just sitting together quietly sharing space". But Jojo has never been given the opportunity to sit quietly with another gorilla. No one knows how Jojo will react to a companion. Moving an animal from an accredited zoo would be a decision for an international committee and based on genetics, health and the animals' personalities and compatibility. Any introduction to another animal would be done very carefully – perhaps giving them an object that smells of the other before they see each other. These slow, cautious ape introductions do happen – when an animal moves from one zoo group to another, for example. Forrester has contacted a number of accredited zoos to explore the possibility of doing this for Jojo. But those discussions have fizzled out with no sign of progress. The problem, she says, is "there aren't clear processes in place to do these kinds of trans-locations". The international rules and processes for moving captive gorillas across international borders - from one zoo or safari park to another - are designed for breeding programmes. "They're not designed for reintroductions into the wild, or to find companions for animals that might need them," says Forrester. And because Jojo, who is probably in his 20s, has reached maturity, King thinks it might be too late for him to bond with other gorillas. "Jojo's situation is unique, but he is probably best where he is," King says, adding that introducing him to another animal could, somewhat ironically, be a source of more stress for him. Being alone is also natural, even relatively common, for mature male gorillas. According to Morrison, about a third of adult males are solitary. "When they reach adolescence, they tend to disperse and spend a good chunk of their life on their own." Solo males will try to persuade females to form a group with them, but some don't succeed and may feel lonely as a consequence, Morrison believes. "If we think of loneliness in an evolutionary context - this mismatch between the social interactions they want and the social interactions they're getting. I suspect feeling lonely is part of the natural, evolutionary drive to attract females." But while those phases – of family life and adult solitude - play a role in wild gorilla society, Jojo was forced into solitary confinement as an infant. Morrison believes Jojo is probably both traumatised and lonely. "[In the wild] gorillas move together, find food together, sleep together," she says. "So much of their lives is just being with this group." That is what Jojo's keepers, Forrester, and others want for Jojo. A friend. Maybe a female, or a compatible male. "It would be good for him to have a companion," says keeper Makaba. "Because being alone is like being cut off from the world - it's like being in prison. "Having another gorilla there would be a good thing for him." Related topics - Published20 April 2025 - Published7 January

news.title: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
news.summary: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
news.summaryTr: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
news.articleText: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test - Published SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage - at about 1515 local time (2115 GMT) on Saturday. It's the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it's splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it's in space. If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than a hundred times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, President of Royal Aeronautical Society. "Full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said. "One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate." - What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? - Published27 October - Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test - Published28 September After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it's not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

news.title: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
news.summary: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans
news.summaryTr: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
news.articleText: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All rescued after cruise ship hit by tanker in New Orleans - Published Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told a news conference. There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans. Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort. The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job". Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations. Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told a news conference. There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans. Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort. The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job". Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations. Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

news.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
news.summary: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.

news.titleTr: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
news.summaryTr: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
news.articleText: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore - Published A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips. Megaspeed is a case in point. It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations. The city-state has had some success in policing this. It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places. They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties. In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore. The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere. Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed. But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department. Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud. In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months. Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case. Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing. In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times. Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses. Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity. On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips. How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness. In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively. For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law. But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities. Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case. BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road. In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed. Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man. During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS. Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences. Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government. All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore. "For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said. Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore". But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips. With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts. Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China. Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said. "Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said. But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China". "This is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour." Additional reporting by Jack Lau of the BBC's Global China Unit. - Published22 hours ago - Published1 day ago

news.titleTr: Çalışma hayatında yeni dönem! 2027-2029 Adil Geçiş Planı yayımlandı
news.summaryTr: Türkiye’nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda hazırlanan Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejisi ve Eylem Planı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genelgesi ile yürürlüğe girdi. Plan kapsamında çalışanların yeni beceriler kazanması, istihdamın korunması ve dönüşümden etkilenen sektör ve bölgelerin desteklenmesi hedef
news.articleText: Çalışma hayatında yeni dönem! 2027-2029 Adil Geçiş Planı yayımlandı - Türkiye'nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda hazırlanan Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejisi ve Eylem Planı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genelgesi ile yürürlüğe girdi. - Plan kapsamında çalışanların yeni beceriler kazanması, istihdamın korunması ve dönüşümden etkilenen sektör ve bölgelerin desteklenmesi hedefleniyor. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’ın imzasını taşıyan genelge, Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 2027-2029 dönemini kapsayan strateji, iklim değişikliği ile yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün çalışma hayatı üzerindeki etkilerini yönetmeyi amaçlıyor. Genelgede, Türkiye’nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda dönüşüm sürecinin kimseyi geride bırakmadan yürütülmesinin önemine dikkat çekildi. 2 Temmuz 2025 tarihli İklim Kanunu ile mevzuata giren adil geçiş yaklaşımının; çalışanların ve işletmelerin değişen koşullara uyum sağlamasını, yeni beceriler kazanmasını, insana yakışır işlerin artırılmasını ve sosyal korumanın güçlendirilmesini gerektirdiği belirtildi. Üç temel politika ekseni belirlendi Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı koordinasyonunda, ilgili paydaşların katılımıyla hazırlanan strateji üç temel eksene dayanıyor: Beceri uyumu: Çalışanların dönüşen iş gücü piyasasının ihtiyaçlarına uygun beceriler kazanması. Kapsayıcı dönüşüm: Yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün farklı sektör, bölge ve toplumsal gruplar üzerindeki etkilerinin gözetilmesi. Sosyal koruma ve toplumsal dayanıklılık: Dönüşüm sürecinde çalışanların ve toplumun desteklenmesi. Plan kapsamında öncelikli sektörlere yönelik sektörel politikalar da uygulanacak. Uygulama altı ayda bir raporlanacak Strateji ve Eylem Planı, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı'nın resmi internet sitesinde yayımlanacak. Planın koordinasyon, izleme ve değerlendirme çalışmaları ilgili kamu kurumları ve sosyal tarafların katılımıyla Bakanlık tarafından yürütülecek. Eylem Planı'nda sorumlu olarak belirlenen kurum ve kuruluşlar, uygulamadaki gelişmeleri altı aylık dönemler halinde Bakanlığa bildirecek. Adil geçiş, düşük karbonlu ve çevre dostu ekonomiye geçiş sırasında çalışanların, işletmelerin ve bölgelerin olumsuz etkilenmesini önlemeyi amaçlayan politika yaklaşımıdır. Temel hedef, yeşil dönüşümün istihdam ve sosyal haklar üzerindeki maliyetlerini azaltırken yeni iş ve beceri fırsatları yaratmaktır.

Sözleşmeli personele disiplin cezaları uygulanacak Yeni düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin disipline aykırı fiil ve davranışlarında devlet memurlarına uygulanan disiplin hükümlerinin kıyasen uygulanması kararlaştırıldı. Buna göre disiplin cezalarının belirlenmesi, yetkili merciler ve disiplin kurullarının işleyişinde memurlara ilişkin hükümler esas alınacak. Aylıktan kesme cezası ise personelin pozisyonuna bağlı ödemelerin toplamı üzerinden 1/30 ile 1/8 arasında uygulanabilecek. Kademe ilerlemesinin durdurulması ve daha ağır cezaları gerektiren fiillerde disiplin kurulu kararı alınacak. Personelin görevine, atamaya yetkili amirin onayıyla son verilebilecek. Hastalık izinleri ve rapor süreleri değişti Hastalık ve refakat izinlerinde, 657 sayılı Kanun'un 105'inci maddesindeki ilgili hükümler sözleşmeli personele de uygulanacak. SGK tarafından ödenen geçici iş göremezlik ödeneği ise personelin ücretinden düşülecek. Azami hastalık izni süresinin tamamlanmasının ardından göreve başlanmaması da sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine ilişkin hükümler arasına eklendi. Göreve başlama sürelerine sınır getirildi Yeni kurallara göre aynı yerde göreve başlayacak personelin, tebliği izleyen iş günü içinde işe başlaması gerekecek. Başka bir yerde görevlendirilen personel ise tebliğ tarihinden itibaren 15 günü izleyen iş günü içinde görevine başlayacak. Belgeyle ispatlanabilen zorlayıcı nedenler dışında bu sürelere uyulmaması, sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine neden olabilecek. Kurum içi yer değişikliğinde 3 yıl şartı 4/B kapsamında çalışan personelin kurum içi yer değişiklikleri de yeniden düzenlendi. Buna göre personelin işe başladığı tarihten itibaren aynı kurumda üç yıllık çalışma süresini tamamlayana kadar yapacağı yer değişikliklerinde belirlenen özel usul ve esaslar uygulanacak. Sözleşmeli personelin görevden uzaklaştırılmasında da devlet memurlarına ilişkin hükümler kıyasen geçerli olacak. Memur kadrosuna geçenlerin boş pozisyonları iptal edilecek Sözleşmeli personelin memur kadrosuna atanması halinde boşalan sözleşmeli personel pozisyonları, başka bir işleme gerek kalmaksızın iptal edilmiş sayılacak. İptal edilen pozisyonlar ilgili kamu personel bilgi sistemine bildirilecek. Eğitim ve ücret ödemelerinde yeni hükümler Düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin temel eğitim, hazırlayıcı eğitim ve staj süreçlerinin görev yaptıkları kurumlar tarafından yürütülmesi kararlaştırıldı. Hizmet içi eğitimlerle personelin mesleki gelişiminin desteklenmesi de öngörüldü. Ücretlerin ay başında peşin ödenmesi uygulaması devam edecek. Ancak ay sonundan önce görevden ayrılan personelden kalan günlere ilişkin ödemeler geri alınacak. Memur kadrosuna atananlar, kendisine aylık bağlananlar ve hayatını kaybeden personel bu uygulamanın dışında tutulacak. Yeni düzenleme, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yayımlanmasıyla yürürlüğe girdi.

news.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT, Jane Street nearly eightfold its Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings while trimming its BlackRock stake, and Trump nominated four SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for Hester Peirce. OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said. The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction. The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems. Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%. The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings. Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million. Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday. The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million). Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems. OpenAI joins a growing field of companies developing payment systems for AI agents. Google introduced its Agent Payments Protocol in 2025, while Visa and Mastercard have launched initiatives to support AI-initiated transactions. Crypto companies are also developing payment infrastructure for AI agents. Coinbase introduced its x402 protocol in 2025, enabling autonomous stablecoin payments for digital services, while Circle launched its Agent Stack in May, allowing agents to hold and spend USDC within predefined limits. Crossmint, which provides stablecoin infrastructure, has taken a different approach, combining stablecoin wallets with traditional card networks. Global agentic commerce transaction value is expected to reach $1.5 trillion by 2030, according to an April report from Juniper Research, up from an estimated $8 billion in 2026. news.title: Adam Back makes case for simpler security as Blockstream launches Bitcoin custody system
news.summary: Blockstream’s new custody system, developed with Thales, uses dedicated hardware for transaction signing as Adam Back advocates for offline security to reduce cyber risks.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Adam Back makes case for simpler security as Blockstream launches Bitcoin custody system
news.summaryTr: Blockstream’s new custody system, developed with Thales, uses dedicated hardware for transaction signing as Adam Back advocates for offline security to reduce cyber risks.
news.articleText: Adam Back makes case for simpler security as Blockstream launches Bitcoin custody system Blockstream’s new custody system, developed with Thales, uses dedicated hardware for transaction signing as Adam Back advocates for offline security to reduce cyber risks. Adam Back’s Bitcoin infrastructure company Blockstream has launched a new institutional digital asset custody solution developed with French technology group Thales, as the cryptographer pushes for simpler, offline security systems to protect Bitcoin against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. The solution, announced Friday, combines Thales’ hardware security modules (HSMs) with Blockstream’s Secure Multi-Party Computation (Secure-MPC) technology, allowing institutions to authorize transactions while keeping sensitive cryptographic operations within dedicated security hardware, according to the company. Unlike conventional MPC implementations that may perform portions of the signing process outside dedicated security hardware, Blockstream said its architecture executes the entire signing protocol within the protected environment of Thales’ HSMs. Blockstream co-founder and CEO Adam Back, a pioneering cryptographer whose Hashcash system helped lay the groundwork for Bitcoin’s proof-of-work mechanism, told Cointelegraph that conventional MPC protocols are often too complex and require too much communication between devices to be practical for fully offline cold storage. “When people talk about MPC, they’re talking about some very esoteric and complicated protocols that are hard to secure and are very interactive. So you can’t really use them in a cold storage setting,” Back said. Related: Blockstream rejects ransom as Liquid hackers hold nearly 600 BTC Adam Back makes the case for simpler Bitcoin custody Back pointed to the Binance $6.3 billion hack as an example of the risks facing internet-connected custody infrastructure, arguing that keeping signing devices offline can help prevent unauthorized access. According to Binance’s investigation, attackers compromised employee devices and obtained credentials that allowed them to access the exchange’s wallet-signing infrastructure. If you connect equipment to the internet, even if it’s via firewalls and so on, there is risk that you can get unauthorized access. You can get hackers into the network, get hackers with access to logins they shouldn’t have and so on. He also said that AI could make existing security challenges more difficult to manage, particularly by helping attackers discover subtle flaws in complex MPC implementations. “The AIs can help attackers find small implementation errors and things like that, which may not be obvious,” he said. Asked whether the broader custody industry would adopt similar offline security models, Back said he hoped so, arguing that institutions should “adapt to the environment” by moving assets into cold storage to reduce exposure to potential AI-assisted attacks. “Complexity is the enemy of security. And going back to basics is the answer, you know, just cold-store it,” Back added. Magazine: NK hackers join memecoin trenches, xStocks adds Hong Kong equities: Asia Express

news.titleTr: SPK'dan iki şirkete bedelsiz sermaye artırımı onayı
news.summaryTr: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek.
news.articleText: SPK'dan iki şirkete bedelsiz sermaye artırımı onayı - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. - İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. SPK bülteninde yer alan karara göre Plastikkart Akıllı Kart İletişim Sistemleri'nin 22 milyon 750 bin TL olan mevcut sermayesi, 277 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 300 milyon TL’ye çıkarılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Flap Kongre Toplantı Hizmetleri'nin ise 93 milyon 750 bin TL olan sermayesi, 306 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 400 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. Böylece iki şirketin sermaye artırımına konu toplam bedelsiz tutarı 583 milyon 500 bin TL olacak. Bedelsiz sermaye artırımı, şirketlerin iç kaynaklarını (yedek akçeler, geçmiş yıl kârları veya sermaye düzeltmesi olumlu farkları gibi) kullanarak sermayelerini artırmasıdır. Bu işlemde yatırımcılar yeni payları ücretsiz alır; hisse sayısı artarken yatırımcının şirketteki ortaklık oranı, diğer koşullar aynı kaldığı sürece değişmez. Hisse fiyatı ise sermaye artırımına bağlı olarak teorik biçimde düzeltilir.
news.articleTextTr: SPK'dan iki şirkete bedelsiz sermaye artırımı onayı - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Plastikkart ve Flap Kongre’nin bedelsiz sermaye artırımlarına onay verdi. - İki şirketin toplam sermayesi 116,5 milyon TL’den 700 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. SPK bülteninde yer alan karara göre Plastikkart Akıllı Kart İletişim Sistemleri'nin 22 milyon 750 bin TL olan mevcut sermayesi, 277 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 300 milyon TL’ye çıkarılacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Flap Kongre Toplantı Hizmetleri'nin ise 93 milyon 750 bin TL olan sermayesi, 306 milyon 250 bin TL bedelsiz artırımla 400 milyon TL’ye yükselecek. Böylece iki şirketin sermaye artırımına konu toplam bedelsiz tutarı 583 milyon 500 bin TL olacak. Bedelsiz sermaye artırımı, şirketlerin iç kaynaklarını (yedek akçeler, geçmiş yıl kârları veya sermaye düzeltmesi olumlu farkları gibi) kullanarak sermayelerini artırmasıdır. Bu işlemde yatırımcılar yeni payları ücretsiz alır; hisse sayısı artarken yatırımcının şirketteki ortaklık oranı, diğer koşullar aynı kaldığı sürece değişmez. Hisse fiyatı ise sermaye artırımına bağlı olarak teorik biçimde düzeltilir.

news.titleTr: ABD'de tüm uçuşlar durduruldu! FAA'dan ülke genelinde kalkış yasağı
news.summaryTr: ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), hava trafik kontrol iletişim sistemlerinde yaşanan ciddi sorunların ardından güvenlik gerekçesiyle ülke genelindeki tüm kalkışları durdurdu. Havada bulunan uçakların inişine izin verilirken yerdeki uçakların yeni bir duyuruya kadar kalkış yapamayacağı bildirildi.
news.articleText: ABD'de tüm uçuşlar durduruldu! FAA'dan ülke genelinde kalkış yasağı - ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), hava trafik kontrol iletişim sistemlerinde yaşanan ciddi sorunların ardından güvenlik gerekçesiyle ülke genelindeki tüm kalkışları durdurdu. - Havada bulunan uçakların inişine izin verilirken yerdeki uçakların yeni bir duyuruya kadar kalkış yapamayacağı bildirildi. FAA, cuma günü yaptığı açıklamada, olağanüstü koşullar ve güvenlik gerekçeleri nedeniyle ülke genelinde kalkışlara yönelik yer durdurma kararı alındığını duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Açıklama öncesinde Chicago'daki hava trafiği de iletişim sorunları nedeniyle durduruldu. Uluslararası uçuşların ise vaka bazında değerlendirileceği belirtildi. Karar, havadaki uçakların inişini engellemiyor ancak yerde bekleyen uçakların kalkış yapmasına izin vermiyor. 11 Eylül'den bu yana ikinci kez Ülke genelindeki tüm kalkışların durdurulması, 11 Eylül 2001 saldırılarından bu yana ikinci kez yaşandı. Daha önce Ocak 2023'te FAA, sistemdeki bir sorun nedeniyle ABD'deki tüm iç hat kalkışlarını iki saatten kısa süreyle durdurmuştu. FAA için 30,1 milyar dolarlık ek kaynak talebi ABD Kongresi, geçen yıl FAA'nın eskiyen iletişim sistemlerinin yenilenmesi için 12,5 milyar dolarlık bütçeyi onaylamıştı. FAA ve Beyaz Saray ise cuma günü diğer sorunların giderilmesi amacıyla Kongre'den ilave 30,1 milyar dolar talep etti. FAA, ABD'de sivil havacılığın güvenliğini ve hava trafik yönetimini düzenleyen federal kurum olarak görev yapıyor. Karar, hava trafik kontrolündeki iletişim altyapısının uçuş güvenliği açısından önemini yeniden gündeme taşıdı.

news.summary: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarına ilişkin yeni bir karar aldı. Kurul, halka açık şirketlerin isteğe bağlı iade mekanizması kapsamında yapacağı ödemelere ilişkin kamuya açıklama, genel kurul ve finansal raporlama esaslarını duyurdu.

news.titleTr: SPK'dan tasfiye edilen fonların iadesine ilişkin yeni karar: Şirketlere açıklama zorunluluğu
news.summaryTr: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarına ilişkin yeni bir karar aldı. Kurul, halka açık şirketlerin isteğe bağlı iade mekanizması kapsamında yapacağı ödemelere ilişkin kamuya açıklama, genel kurul ve finansal raporlama esaslarını duyurdu.
news.articleText: SPK'dan tasfiye edilen fonların iadesine ilişkin yeni karar: Şirketlere açıklama zorunluluğu YAYIN TARİHİ, 14 Kasım 2026 00:17 GÜNCELLEME, 14 Kasım 2026 01:18 PAYLAŞ - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarına ilişkin yeni bir karar aldı. - Kurul, halka açık şirketlerin isteğe bağlı iade mekanizması kapsamında yapacağı ödemelere ilişkin kamuya açıklama, genel kurul ve finansal raporlama esaslarını duyurdu. SPK, tasfiye edilen yatırım fonlarından elde edilen kazançların halka açık şirketler tarafından isteğe bağlı olarak iade edilmesine ilişkin esasları belirledi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İadelerin hisse fiyatını veya yatırımcı kararlarını etkileyebilecek nitelikte olması halinde özel durum açıklaması yapılacak. Kurulun duyurduğu ilkelere göre şirketler, söz konusu iade ödemelerini genel kurul toplantılarında ayrı bir gündem maddesiyle pay sahiplerinin bilgisine sunacak. Ödemelerin finansal tablolara nasıl yansıtılacağı ve dipnotlarda nasıl açıklanacağı ise Türkiye Muhasebe ve Finansal Raporlama Standartları çerçevesinde değerlendirilecek.

news.title: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
news.summary: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption
news.summaryTr: Experts say the event is a "stark reminder" of how heavily the world relies on a small group of big tech providers.
news.articleText: Microsoft 'deeply sorry' for global outage after almost 24 hours of disruption - Published Microsoft has said it is "deeply sorry" for the service outage to its products, including Outlook and Teams, which has caused disruption around the world. Services were broadly recovering by Friday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after issues began. Microsoft said it was making "encouraging progress", but added it does not know when services will fully recover. The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users. More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide. Microsoft said it was a technical issue introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or artificial intelligence agents. Experts said the event was a "stark reminder" of how heavily businesses and vital services rely on a small group of big tech providers. Users began reporting they were having trouble accessing Microsoft 365 products on Thursday. By Friday, the far-reaching issue was affecting institutions from the Japanese government and the Philippines Supreme Court to the Australian spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. - Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost? - Published5 hours ago - Courts, spies and MPs: How the Microsoft outage has been felt around the world - Published6 hours ago In the UK, some parts of the NHS, including GPs and hospitals, were affected, as were some schools and police forces. UK cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the incident had "limited" impact on critical frontline services such as 999 calls, and there had been no disruption to the transport network. In Canada, however, the national rail network said passengers may not be able to receive email updates about their trips, and hospitals across the country also had issues with emails. In the US, staff members from the House of Representatives told Politico it had set back an entire day of legislative work as everything was on Microsoft's Outlook. Singapore's government acknowledged some of its systems had been impacted, and in India, the outage disrupted work for many on Friday. In Turkey, advisers and officials attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya were left frustrated by being unable to access Outlook. The issues also affected smaller businesses and individuals. Peter Pentz, a winemaker in South Africa, said his entire business was basically brought to a "standstill". His winery's communication with exports was also brought to a standstill, he said, and "critical production work" was been halted as the Cape West Coast winery "relies on these systems for parts of our day-to-day operations". Georgia from Staffordshire in England said she was due to complete her first house purchase today after waiting eight months to get to this point - but the outage has delayed that. "The solicitor mentioned there may be a delay due to not being able to contact other agencies. "We're not the only one completing today, there are hundreds of houses and for them to ring everyone in time is unfeasible," Georgia said. 'Encouraging recovery signals' Microsoft first acknowledged users in the Americas were unable to access Exchange Online mailboxes at 17:54 GMT on Thursday, and shortly after warned the disruption was possibly affecting Microsoft 365 globally. While it launched an investigation and engineers began working to restore services, by 04:36 on Friday Microsoft was reporting only a "partial recovery" in some parts of the world. By 13:32, the tech giant said there were "broader improvements" in North America, "sustained improvements" across much of Europe and "encouraging recovery signals" in the Asia Pacific region. Microsoft said it restored services gradually due to the scale of the problem and to help ensure services remain stable once they are up and running again. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners," a Microsoft spokesperson said. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously." Microsoft said it has no "ETA" for when services will be fully recovered. A full post-incident report will be released once Microsoft has completed a review. Experts said while workers may have been happy to not have email access for the day, the incident showed the dependence many organisations have on these cloud-based services. "The global Microsoft outage is a stark reminder of how heavily we rely on a handful of big tech providers," said Rob Demain, chief executive of cybersecurity firm e2e-assure. Matt Saunders, field chief technology officer at tech consultancy Adaptavist, said it would be challenging to mitigate against a similar problem. "Classic IT disaster planning strategies suggest using a second service for resilience, but in practice, it's almost impossible for a business to function without tools such as Microsoft," he said. "In the wake of this outage, organisations must have a plan in place for how to work without such tools, for when incidents like this occur." news.summaryTr: Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), EDATA, KARCL ve GRTHO pay piyasalarındaki işlemler nedeniyle kapsamlı yaptırım kararı aldı. Kurul, 65 kişi ve 6 şirkete 2 yıl süreyle işlem yasağı getirirken 76 kişi hakkında da suç duyurusunda bulunulmasına karar verdi.
news.articleText: SPK'dan 3 hisseye çifte yaptırım! 65 kişi ve 6 şirkete işlem yasağı - Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), EDATA, KARCL ve GRTHO pay piyasalarındaki işlemler nedeniyle kapsamlı yaptırım kararı aldı. - Kurul, 65 kişi ve 6 şirkete 2 yıl süreyle işlem yasağı getirirken 76 kişi hakkında da suç duyurusunda bulunulmasına karar verdi. SPK'nın incelemeleri sonucunda EDATA, KARCL ve GRTHO hisselerinde gerçekleştirilen işlemlerin piyasa dolandırıcılığı kapsamında değerlendirildiği belirtildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kurul, söz konusu işlemlerle bağlantılı olarak hem gerçek kişiler hem de şirketler hakkında yaptırım uyguladı. 65 kişi ve 6 şirkete 2 yıl işlem yasağı SPK kararına göre EDATA işlemleri nedeniyle 8, KARCL işlemleri nedeniyle 44, GRTHO işlemleri nedeniyle 24 kişi hakkında işlem yasağı kararı verildi. Birden fazla dosyada adı geçen kişiler bulunduğundan, toplam 76 kayda karşılık 65 farklı kişiye 2 yıl süreyle işlem yasağı getirildi. Karar kapsamında 6 şirkete de ilgili paylarda kendi nam ve hesaplarına gerçekleştirdikleri işlemlerle sınırlı olmak üzere 2 yıl işlem yasağı uygulandı. Bu şirketler A1 Capital Portföy Yönetimi, A1 Capital Yatırım Menkul Değerler, Pardus Portföy Yönetimi, Tera Girişim Sermayesi Yatırım Ortaklığı, Tera Portföy Yönetimi ve Tera Yatırım Bankası oldu. Etkin pişmanlık için 15 gün süre Kurul, hakkında suç duyurusu kararı alınan kişilerin Kanun'un 107/3'üncü maddesi kapsamında etkin pişmanlık hükümlerinden yararlanabileceğini bildirdi. Buna göre, bu hükümlerden yararlanmak isteyenlerin, 500 bin TL'den az olmamak üzere elde ettikleri veya elde edilmesine neden oldukları menfaatin iki katı tutarındaki parayı SPK kararından itibaren 15 gün içinde Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı'nın ilgili hesabına yatırmaları gerekiyor. Ödeme belgelerinin de aynı süre içinde SPK'ya iletilmesi şartı bulunuyor.
